title: Signal Bridge: Incident communications playbook and status templates (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, usable draft of incident communications for the Signal Bridge (internal name for oncall->stakeholder comms). Goal: give oncall a minimal checklist + copy-ready templates for status page entries and customer-facing messages so we spend less time drafting and more time fixing.

Notes to reader:
- This is intentionally concise and slightly informal — meant for war-room copy-paste.
- Use the variables: {{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{SEVERITY}}, {{ETA}}, {{ROOT_CAUSE}}, {{MITIGATION}}, {{NEXT_UPDATE}}.
- Channel: #ops-signal-bridge for coordination; page watchers = product owners + comms + legal on high-sev.

Severity translation table (for comms tone):
- Sev 1 / Sev A (system-wide, customer-visible outage): urgent, transparent, frequent updates (every 15–30m). Use direct "We are experiencing" language. No speculation.
- Sev 2 (partial degradation, subset of requests / regions): measured updates (every 30–60m), indicate affected scope, mitigation progress.
- Sev 3 (minor impact, rate-limit errors, intermittent): single post to status + follow-up at incident close.

Internal war-room checklist (first 30 minutes):
1) Join bridge and confirm incident record: create JIRA SRE ticket if not already (format SRE-{{YYYY}}-xxxxx).
2) Post initial note to #ops-signal-bridge with one-line summary + pointer to ticket + runbook link. Example: "SRE-2025-1034: svc-infer-eu high latency for 2025-11-05 14:12 UTC. Join bridge: <link>. Initial hypothesis: CUDA OOM on pool-3."
3) Assign roles (primary responder, comms lead, mitigation lead, customer liaison). Quick round-robin if unsure.
4) Set cadence for updates and owner for the next update.
5) Draft initial status page entry using template A (below) and post as pending (not public) for review by comms lead.
6) If external impact > threshold (see SLA table), notify customer-success and legal.

Quick internal checklist items (ongoing):
- Capture command outputs and timestamps in the ticket.
- Avoid speculation; tag any unconfirmed hypotheses as "hypothesis".
- Keep a running timeline in ticket body (times in UTC).
- If rollback is considered, capture decision and approver in ticket.

Status page templates (choose appropriate severity):
Template A — Outage (Sev1):
Title: Degraded service: Redwood inference API - ({{AFFECTED_REGIONS}})
Impact: We are currently experiencing elevated latency and errors affecting text generation and chat APIs in {{AFFECTED_REGIONS}}. A subset of requests may fail or time out.
Current status: Investigating — Our engineering team is actively investigating.
Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}}
Actions we are taking: Engineers are working to identify the root cause and apply mitigations to restore normal operation.
Reference: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} (internal)

Template B — Partial degradation (Sev2):
Title: Partial service degradation for embeddings endpoints
Impact: Some customers may observe increased response times from the embeddings endpoints in us-west-2. The issue appears to affect queued/batched jobs and does not impact hosted API auth or billing.
Status: Mitigation in progress — we have deployed a temporary routing change that should reduce queuing; monitoring for stabilization.
ETA: {{ETA}}
Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}}

Template C — Informational (Sev3):
Title: Maintenance notice / Intermittent errors observed
Impact: Intermittent 502 errors for a small percentage of requests. Not customer-facing for most accounts.
Status: Monitoring
Resolution: If resolved, update to "Resolved" and include root cause summary.

Customer-facing email/snippet templates (short, polite, non-technical):
Template 1 — Immediate outage alert (to affected customers):
Subject: Service disruption affecting Redwood inference - incident {{INCIDENT_ID}}
Body: Hello — we’re contacting you because we detected an issue that may affect your API requests to Redwood Inference. We are actively investigating and working to restore normal operation. We will update you by {{NEXT_UPDATE}}. If you see specific errors in logs please share request ids and timestamps and we’ll prioritize. Apologies for the disruption. — The Redwood SRE team

Template 2 — Follow-up (mitigation / temporary workaround):
Subject: Update on incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — mitigation in place
Body: Hello — we implemented a mitigation (temporary routing / scaled-up pool) that should reduce failed requests. Please monitor; we plan a full resolution and a post-incident summary. If you continue to see errors after {{ETA}}, please reply with examples. — Redwood Ops

Template 3 — Post-incident summary (customer):
Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} resolved — summary and impact
Body: Hello — Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} that occurred on {{DATE}} is now resolved. Impact: Customers in {{AFFECTED_REGIONS}} may have experienced higher latency and occasional failed requests between {{START_TIME}} and {{END_TIME}}. Root cause: {{ROOT_CAUSE}}. What we did: {{MITIGATION}}. Actions to prevent recurrence: {{FOLLOW_UP_ACTIONS}}. If you have further questions, contact support@redwood.ai.

Internal language & dos-don'ts for comms lead:
- DO be direct and factual; "We are investigating" is better than overconfident guesses.
- DO indicate scope (percent traffic, regions, customer tiers).
- DO escalate copy to legal on any incident involving data leakage.
- DON'T commit to timelines you don't control (avoid "we expect full recovery in 5 minutes" unless mitigation is concrete).
- DON'T share internal-only debug logs on public status page.

War-room timeline template (example):
T+0: initial detection, ticket created, roles assigned, initial status entry drafted (private).
T+10: first internal update: what we know, initial mitigation steps taken.
T+30: publish public status page (if customer visible) and send customer alert.
T+60: publish mitigation update with ETA if available.
T+resolution: publish resolution + short RCA stub within 24 hours; full RCA within 5 business days for Sev1.

Escalation contacts (primary order):
1) Oncall SRE (primary) — see rota.
2) SRE lead: Diego Morales
3) Product owner oncall (for affected product area) — ping @product-oncall
4) Customer success manager — Priya Nair
5) Legal (if data exposure suspected) — legal-oncall@redwood.ai

Quick copy checklist before publishing customer-facing content:
- Replace placeholders, localize time to UTC, include incident id.
- Confirm scope (all customers vs subset).
- Confirm non-sensitive wording (no stack traces or internal IPs).
- Run by comms lead (or product owner for major incidents).

Post-incident follow-up (SLA for comms):
- Within 1 hour of resolution: publish an initial "resolved" entry summarizing high level fixes.
- Within 24 hours: post short RCA stub to the ticket and to status page as an update.
- Within 5 business days (Sev1): publish full RCA with timeline, root cause, and preventative actions.

Outstanding questions / TODOs for this playbook (notes to self):
- Add exact SLA thresholds for automated customer notifications (TBD with product).
- Template translations for non-English customers (priority: JA, DE).
- Decide whether to auto-post status page entries from Sentry/monitoring (danger: noise).
- Add pre-approved legal phrasing for PII/Data exposures.

Appendix: useful snippet bank (copy-paste)
- "Investigating: We have identified increased latency impacting requests to {{SERVICE}}. Engineers are working on mitigation; next update in 30 minutes."
- "Mitigation deployed: We scaled pool capacity and applied a temporary routing change; error rate reduced by ~70%. Monitoring for stability."
- "Resolved: The service is operating normally. We’ll publish an RCA within 5 business days."

Contacts + quick links:
- Incident board: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-queue
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.ai/ (ops login required)
- War-room channel: #ops-signal-bridge

If this draft looks okay, next steps: finalize wording with Product/Comms, add legal-approved templates for data incidents, and run a tabletop next month to validate timings.

End of draft.
